title: Build an app that includes text analysis
learningObjective: Build a lightweight application that includes text analysis with Azure Language in Foundry Tools or a model prompt with structured output.
foundation: A text analysis app sends text to a service and uses the results: for example, flag angry reviews, route support tickets, or redact phone numbers.
Two ways to do it: call Azure Language's prebuilt features (consistent results with confidence scores), or prompt a generative model to return the analysis as JSON (flexible).
engineer: Azure Language Python SDK (azure-ai-textanalytics): TextAnalyticsClient(endpoint, credential) with analyze_sentiment(docs, show_opinion_mining=True), extract_key_phrases, recognize_entities, recognize_pii_entities (redacted_text), detect_language; begin_analyze_actions for several actions or summarization in one long-running call.
Results are per document with IDs, confidence scores and errors; batch up to the documented limits per request; handle per-document errors.
Model approach: responses.create with instructions describing the fields and a JSON schema (structured output), for example {sentiment, product, refund_requested}. Validate the JSON before using it.

Design: detect language first, redact PII before storing, threshold on confidence, and log only what you need. Authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID (Cognitive Services User role) or keys in Key Vault.

example.title: Ticket triage
body: A support team's app calls Azure Language to detect language and redact PII, then gets sentiment and key phrases for a dashboard.
For a custom field ('Is the customer asking for a refund?'), it prompts a chat model to return JSON with refund_requested: true/false.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with access to Microsoft Foundry (ai.azure.com)
permissions: Azure AI User on the Foundry project to use models and agents; Azure AI Project Manager or Owner to create projects and deployments
limits: Model availability differs by region and deployment type
Deployments have tokens-per-minute (TPM) rate limits and quota per subscription and region
portal: Foundry portal > Language playground: test features and copy the endpoint.
Assign Cognitive Services User (or Azure AI User) to the app identity.

configuration.python:
# pip install azure-ai-textanalytics azure-identity
import os
from azure.ai.textanalytics import TextAnalyticsClient
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

client = TextAnalyticsClient(endpoint=os.environ["LANGUAGE_ENDPOINT"], credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
reviews = ["The battery life is fantastic, but the screen scratches far too easily."]

for doc in client.analyze_sentiment(reviews, show_opinion_mining=True):
    print(doc.sentiment, doc.confidence_scores)
    for sentence in doc.sentences:
        for opinion in sentence.mined_opinions:
            print(" ", opinion.target.text, "->", opinion.target.sentiment)

print([p for p in client.extract_key_phrases(reviews)[0].key_phrases])
print([(e.text, e.category) for e in client.recognize_entities(reviews)[0].entities])
print(client.recognize_pii_entities(["Call me on 555-0142"])[0].redacted_text)

troubleshooting.symptom: Some documents return errors while others succeed.
troubleshooting.fix: Check each result's is_error and handle it.
Use structured output with a JSON schema and validate.

comparisons.difference: Language: fixed features, scores, low cost per item. Model: flexible, custom fields, needs validation.

misconceptions.reality: Combine them: prebuilt for standard tasks, a model for custom ones.

architectureDecisions: Use prebuilt features for sentiment, PII and entities.
Use a model for custom classification.
